accepted.title: Cascade Spirocyclization–Difunctionalization or Rearrangement of Bicyclobutyl-Tethered Aldehyde Hydrazones via Strain Release
accepted.titleZh: 应变释放驱动的双环丁烷连接醛腙级联螺环化-双官能化或重排
accepted.reason: Develops divergent strain-release synthetic methodology from bicyclobutyl-tethered aldehyde hydrazones, including cascade spirocyclization–difunctionalization and a three-component rearrangement, with diverse products, scale-up, and complex-substrate demonstrations.
accepted.evidenceBasis: Crossref publisher abstract reports diverse halo-succinimide-containing diazaspiro[3.3]heptan-3-ones and halo-sulfoximine-featured cyclobutane carboxamides from two related reaction manifolds, plus scaled-up experiments and complex substrates.
accepted.challengeReason: Although mechanistic studies are also presented, the primary contribution is a preparative reaction platform with product diversity, multi-component scope, scale-up, and complex-substrate application, so it clearly meets the Gallery methodology criterion.

rejected.title: Cyclodextrin‐Directed Assembly of Dynamic Polyoxometalate Pseudo‐Rotaxanes
rejected.reason: Supramolecular/inorganic polyoxometalate cluster reorganization and host–guest assembly rather than a general organic or polymer synthesis methodology.
rejected.evidenceBasis: The abstract centers on α-cyclodextrin-directed reorganization of Mo6/Mo12 polyoxometalate clusters into pseudo-rotaxanes, characterized by NMR/ITC and crystallography; the synthetic objective is adaptive inorganic supramolecular architecture.
rejected.challengeReason: It does synthesize new assemblies, but the generalizable advance is inorganic cluster self-assembly rather than preparative organic/polymer reaction methodology, so inclusion would broaden the Gallery beyond its defined scope.

rejected.title: Hydrogen‐Bond Encoding in a Structurally Minimal Cyclochiral Monomer Enables Assembly of Large Cavities Displaying Supramolecular Isomerism
rejected.reason: Supramolecular host–guest self-assembly and molecular-recognition study; no general preparative organic reaction or polymerization method is developed.
rejected.evidenceBasis: The abstract focuses on hydrogen-bond-encoded monomers assembling into fullerene-binding tetrameric capsules, guest-induced self-sorting, supramolecular isomerism, and recognition/catalysis potential.
rejected.challengeReason: The work uses a designed organic monomer, but the central advance is noncovalent assembly behavior, not a broadly applicable covalent synthesis or polymerization methodology.

rejected.title: Janus Covalent Organic Framework Films With Macroscopic Directional Carrier Migration for Switchable Gas Sensing
rejected.reason: COF film/device materials research centered on directional carrier migration and gas sensing, without a general organic/polymer synthesis methodology.
rejected.evidenceBasis: The abstract emphasizes sequence-controlled Janus COF films, built-in electric fields, carrier migration, and enhanced NO2/NH3 sensing performance.
rejected.challengeReason: Although COF construction is synthetic, it is a specific materials fabrication step supporting device/sensing performance rather than a broadly transferable synthesis method.

rejected.title: Single‐Atom O/S/Se Substitution at the Glycosidic Linkage in Glycopeptide Cancer Vaccines Reveals Divergent Performance
rejected.reason: Chemical-biology/vaccine structure–function study using defined glycopeptide analogues; the main advance is biological performance, not a general synthetic methodology.
rejected.evidenceBasis: The abstract mentions streamlined access to Se-linked Tn glycopeptides, but most of the study concerns antigen recognition, molecular dynamics, STD-NMR, vaccine conjugation, antibody response, and therapeutic efficacy.
rejected.challengeReason: The synthetic access is enabling rather than the central generalized methodological contribution; there is no demonstrated broad reaction/substrate platform comparable to the Gallery's synthesis-method criterion.

rejected.title: Tailoring Local Anion Chemistry Affinity Enables Stable Halide–Sulfide Interfaces and Fast Ion Transport in Dual‐Electrolyte all‐Solid‐State Batteries
rejected.reason: All-solid-state battery electrolyte/interface materials research, outside organic-synthesis methodology scope.
rejected.evidenceBasis: The abstract centers on sulfurized halide electrolytes, halide–sulfide interface stabilization, Li+ conductivity, cycling performance, and areal capacity.
rejected.challengeReason: The chemistry modifies inorganic electrolyte materials and battery interfaces; it does not develop a preparative organic or polymer synthesis method.

qualityControl.note: Every accepted and high-priority rejected candidate received an adversarial challenge pass; normal-priority rejections also received explicit challenge review in this batch.
